subject: Civil Engineering
title: Dam Decommissioning and Removal
description: A quick, practical guide to Dam Decommissioning and Removal.

hook.text: Sometimes the best thing for a dam is to take it down — let the river flow free again.

buildup.text: Removal restores fish migration, sediment transport, and natural flood cycles.

discovery.text: Sediment trapped behind the dam must be managed — releasing it all at once would smother downstream.

twist.text: Removal of Washington's Elwha dams in 2014 restored salmon runs dormant for a century.

climax.text: Within three years, the river rebuilt its delta — nature reclaimed what the dam had changed.

punchline.text: Some dams outlived their purpose. Removing them gives the river a second chance.

quiz.question: What happened after the Elwha dams were removed in Washington state?
options: Severe flooding destroyed downstream communities within months
Salmon runs returned and the river rebuilt its delta within three years
The river dried up because it no longer had a reservoir to store water

details.summary: Dam removal is the controlled demolition of a dam that has reached the end of its useful life, poses unacceptable safety risk, or causes environmental harm that outweighs its benefits.
details.whyItMatters: Over 1,700 dams have been removed in the United States alone as communities recognize that some aging dams cost more to maintain than the benefits they provide. Dam removal is a growing trend worldwide.
takeaways: Dam removal restores natural river flow, fish migration, and sediment transport
Sediment management is the biggest engineering challenge during dam removal
Cost of maintaining an aging, obsolete dam often exceeds removal cost

faq.question: What happens to all the sediment trapped behind a dam when it is removed?
faq.answer: Sediment release is the primary concern during dam removal. Gradual or staged removal allows sediment to erode slowly, reducing downstream impacts. Some projects dredge contaminated sediment before removal. River channels re-establish through the former reservoir.

faq.question: How quickly do river ecosystems recover after dam removal?
faq.answer: Physical channel recovery occurs within months to years. Fish populations can rebound within one to five years as migration routes reopen. Riparian vegetation colonizes the former reservoir floor within three to ten years.
